videos.script: Almost every connection starts with a question. What is the address of this name? {{ask}} On most small networks, every machine asks somebody outside. The firm never sees the question. {{resolver}} In this lesson the firm gets its own resolver. Every machine asks it, and it writes every question down. {{list}} Then the resolver gets a list. For a name on the list, it lies on purpose. Sometimes it says the name does not exist. Sometimes it sends the program to an address you own. {{sinkhole}} That address is a sinkhole. Whatever the program meant to fetch arrives there instead, with the name of the machine that sent it. {{limits}} And you will see where the control stops: a program that asks somebody else, and the switch rule that stops it from asking.
